query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Incorporating ~0.25 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles into the CoCrFeNi matrix will create an oxide dispersion-strengthened alloy that forms a stable, self-healing oxide film during sliding, thereby maintaining a low coefficient of friction and reduced wear rate across the full temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C.
generation.material_initial_state: CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy matrix without added dispersoids
generation.intervention: Introduce ~0.25 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles into the alloy during processing to form a uniformly dispersed oxide phase
generation.conditions: Sliding wear tests conducted in ambient air under controlled loads at temperatures from room temperature up to 800 °C
generation.structural_mediator: Uniformly dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles that induce grain refinement and dispersion strengthening while promoting the formation of a protective and self-healing oxide layer during sliding
generation.mechanism: The Y2O3 nanoparticles act as pinning sites that stabilize grain boundaries and enhance the overall hardness and high-temperature strength of the matrix. During sliding, the interaction with oxygen leads to the formation of a thin, adherent oxide film. This film repairs itself during intermittent sliding cycles, reducing direct metal-to-metal contact and thereby lowering friction and wear across a broad temperature range.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the unmodified CoCrFeNi alloy, the Y2O3-modified composite is expected to exhibit a consistently lower friction coefficient and significantly reduced wear rates throughout the testing regime, especially at elevated temperatures near 800 °C.
generation.baseline: Performance metrics (friction coefficient and wear rate) observed for the standard CoCrFeNi alloy under identical sliding conditions without Y2O3 addition
generation.boundary: Temperature: room temperature to 800 °C; Load: moderate sliding loads typical of tribological testing; Environment: ambient air
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of friction and wear improvements is uncertain without empirical data, and potential microstructural interactions at extreme conditions may vary the effectiveness of the self-healing oxide film.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of CoCrFeNi samples: one with ~0.25 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles and one without (control). Conduct systematic sliding wear tests across the temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C under identical loads in ambient air. Characterize the friction coefficient, wear rate, and surface morphology (including oxide film formation) using tribometers and microscopy techniques.
measurements: Coefficient of friction at various temperatures
Wear volume loss or rate under sliding conditions
Surface analysis (SEM/EDS, XPS) to verify the presence and integrity of the protective oxide film
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Y2O3-modified samples do not show statistically significant reductions in the friction coefficient and wear rate compared to the control samples across the full temperature range, or if a stable, self-healing oxide film is not observed on the modified samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The microstructural, mechanical, and tribological properties of oxide dispersion strengthened CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloys composites were investigated. Based on the analysis and tests, the following conclusions are drawn. A new ODS-CrMnFeCoNi HEA matrix composite was successfully prepared from elemental powders by using MA and SPS. The as-milled HEA powders exhibited FCC phase and BCC phase. After sintering, the composite material consists of a single FCC structure and Y2O3 nanoparticles in homogeneous dispersion state. With increasing content of Y2O3, only 0.25 wt % Y2O3 nanoparticles can improve the strength to 1000 MPa, which was 15.2% higher than the CrMnFeCoNi matrix. Additionally, the strain also increased from 5.4% to 6.1%. This is mainly because of the grain boundary strengthening effect, orowan looping, and load transfer effect. However, with 0.5 wt % Y2O3 nanoparticles, both the strength and strain were decreased, and this may contributed to some complicated reasons. The addition of Y2O3 nanoparticles increased the hardness of alloy, from 246 HV to 403 HV and 311 HV, respectively. reading.lever: Incorporate ~0.25 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles into the CoCrFeNi matrix to form a stable, dispersion-strengthened microstructure with self-healing oxide films.
reading.why: ODS via Y2O3 has demonstrated improved high-temperature wear resistance and reduced friction in related HEA systems, offering a promising solution for full-range sliding performance.
